requirements.statement: The notification type question offers radio options in this order, with no hint text and none pre-selected on a new start: Live animals; Germinal products (semen, ova, embryos); Plants for planting; Potatoes (seed and ware); Wood products. Live animals continues to the animals frontend's live-animals start, which creates the GBN-AG draft with the live-animals category and lands on its origin page. Germinal products continues to the start of the germinal products set, the live-animals set's sibling in the animals frontend, which creates its own GBN-AG draft with the germinal products category and lands on that set's origin page; this option may land before the germinal products set itself is built. Plants for planting, Potatoes (seed and ware) and Wood products continue to the start of the high-risk plants journey in trade-imports-plants-frontend, which creates a plants draft and lands on plants' own first page.
requirements.why: The target design's options and order, with each type sent to the real service or set that takes it: the real services split journeys by type, each creating its own draft and reference (c-007). The 9 October ruling offers Germinal products second and makes it start the germinal products set, each set passing its category when it creates the draft, and lets the link land ahead of the set. The templates ruling gives plants the same entry from the INS type question.

conflicts.about: Whether the ruling's real-constraint override covers accessibility and no-JavaScript use, wherever Design Release 2.1's markup or behaviour falls short of a GOV.UK accessibility pattern the real service follows.

positions.says: Every page works fully without JavaScript, and CSS and JavaScript may only enhance a page that already works.
c-006's clause that the origin control matches the prototype's search icon and search behaviour is replaced: hint and placeholder follow the prototype, the rest follows the component.
On transit countries, adding a country the moment it is picked, removing one without a page load and the custom announcement wording wait on design, replacing c-006's transit clause.
The transporter list's in-page filter is blocked with transporter management, replacing c-006's transporters clause on the filter.
The CPH page's digit filtering and paste spreading wait on design, replacing c-006's CPH clause.
The commercial transporter's fields hidden behind the address search wait on design and on the address lookup.
Success banners stay until the trader leaves or reloads the page, because WCAG 2.2.1 rules out a message that leaves on a timer.
Only a DR1 judgement or a real constraint (persistence, validation, auth, cross-service) overrides the prototype.
The ruling does not say whether a constrained service keeps today's behaviour or matches the prototype as closely as it can.
The origin page keeps its title in an error state, with no 'Error: ' prefix.
The country search box has no label; the 'Country of origin' heading is not associated with it.
The region code input is not linked to its hint or error.
The country search is a custom component outside the GOV.UK toolbox.
In an error state the browser title is prefixed 'Error: '.

conflicts.outcome: The real-constraint override covers accessibility and no-JavaScript use, and reaches only as far as that duty: every page follows Design Release 2.1 except where it falls short of it. The 9 October afternoon ruling, which outranks every other source, makes every page work fully without JavaScript and replaces this conflict's earlier origin, transit, transporter and CPH clauses. Origin: keep the 'Error: ' title prefix, a real 'Country of origin' label on an accessible-autocomplete over a native select that works without JavaScript, and the region code input linked to its hint and error with the error style; within that build the hint and placeholder follow Design Release 2.1, while opening on focus, matching, the arrow and the announcements follow the component as the real frontend configures it (c-009). Port of entry and transit countries: keep today's native selects, the Add country button and the Remove buttons that submit the form, and today's announcements; adding a country the moment it is picked, removing one without a page load and the custom announcement wording wait on design question 4; keep the 'Error: ' title prefix and the visually hidden country name on each Remove. Transporters: the list's in-page filter is blocked with transporter management, and the commercial form's fields hidden behind the address search wait on design question 10 and on the address lookup; without JavaScript the commercial form shows its fields from the start. Upload documents: keep the 'Error: ' title prefix, the error summary at the top of the main content, the attachment error after its hint, Remove buttons naming their document and link text saying it opens in a new tab; everything else follows Design Release 2.1. CPH number: the page works as today with the server's checks, and the digit filtering and paste spreading wait on design question 7. Viewed notification: the title is '<reference> - Import notification service - GOV.UK' in every state, and the journey review keeps 'Review your notification - Import notification service - GOV.UK'. Success banners (the notification list's, the deletion message and the templates pages'): no auto-dismiss; a banner stays until the trader leaves or reloads the page, and everything else about it follows Design Release 2.1.

conflicts.outcome: The 9 October afternoon ruling, which outranks every other source, replaces the earlier outcome that took the prototype's copy and behaviour wholesale. The country of origin control stays the real frontend's accessible-autocomplete over a native select. Built now, in both animals sets and, in the same increment, in plants: no hint (req-015) and the placeholder 'Search for a country' (req-016), with the component's own result and selection announcements (req-start-and-origin-002). Opening on focus, how typed text matches, how matches are shown and the arrow follow the component as the real frontend configures it, so req-017 and req-019 are not built, and the box's look belongs to EUDPA-635 (req-start-and-origin-001). The separate 'Search' button (req-018) waits on design question 1, and the prototype's custom announcement wording (req-020) on design question 13; both change plants when built. Plants keeps its own list, guidance and errors; d-015's mirroring of the animals hint gives way to the ruling with the animals hint itself, and p9-049 is not overruled because it still backs plants' label and error (req-start-and-origin-006). Today's claims are not overruled: they are the evidence of what each change replaces.
